doc.purpose: Global screen-shader manifest: stages the pinned libretro shader tree and emits Semu-owned screen preset wrappers.

doc.why: lcd-grid-v2 lights each output pixel from its 2x2 source neighbours through texelFetchOffset, and a fetch past the source's edge returns black, so the outermost row and column of every edge pixel were drawn darker (the GBC and GBA default looks, the DS and 3DS grid looks). wrap_mode cannot reach a fetch. The patch clamps the fetched texel onto the source, as clamp_to_edge does for a sampled read: an edge pixel's outside neighbour is itself, every in-range fetch is unchanged, so the interior is identical.
doc.provenance: libretro/slang-shaders 4812a82f6c9a11cc8b5a7447040a98c9fc80c00e, handheld/shaders/lcd-cgwg/lcd-grid-v2.slang (cgwg's LCD grid); only its fetch_offset macro changes.

doc.why: The authentic GBC pass samples the four nearest source texels through its sampler, and the preset leaves pass 1 at the default clamp_to_border, so past the edge it read black and the outermost row and column of every edge pixel were darker. wrap_mode1 clamp_to_edge makes the outside neighbour the edge texel; samples inside the picture are unchanged.
doc.provenance: libretro/slang-shaders 4812a82f6c9a11cc8b5a7447040a98c9fc80c00e, handheld/authentic_gbc.slangp (fishku, CC0); one line added.

doc.why: The DMG look draws its backlight paper (a 1024x1024 texture) across the picture with a linear filter and the default clamp_to_border. Once the picture is wider or taller than the paper (7x, 1120x1008 on 1920x1080), the outermost line's filter reaches past the paper's edge and blends its black border in: up to 7 levels darker on the right edge and 4 on the top. BACKGROUND_wrap_mode clamp_to_edge keeps that line on the paper; every sample inside it is unchanged.
doc.provenance: libretro/slang-shaders 4812a82f6c9a11cc8b5a7447040a98c9fc80c00e, handheld/gameboy.slangp (Harlequin's Game Boy shader); one line added, and a final newline.

doc.why: The pocket look draws its paper (2048x2048) the same way. It stays inside the paper up to 12x, so nothing changes at 1280x800 or 1920x1080 (5x and 7x); the same line keeps a larger screen's outermost line off the black border.
doc.provenance: libretro/slang-shaders 4812a82f6c9a11cc8b5a7447040a98c9fc80c00e, handheld/gameboy-pocket.slangp (Harlequin's Game Boy shader); one line added, and a final newline.

doc.why: The AGB-001 look draws its 4x pattern and then scales it to the viewport with a linear filter (stock.slang), whose footprint at the outermost output pixels reaches past the edge into the default clamp_to_border black. wrap_mode1 clamp_to_edge keeps those taps on the picture; every footprint inside it is unchanged.
doc.provenance: libretro/slang-shaders 4812a82f6c9a11cc8b5a7447040a98c9fc80c00e, handheld/agb001.slangp (mGBA's AGB-001 shader); one line added.

doc.why: DMG palette and temporal LCD response with a crisp dot matrix for the declared 160x144, 10:9 game surface; real-device appearance remains a physical acceptance gate.
Pinned libretro Game Boy Pocket palette, paper background, LCD matrix, and temporal response provide a materially distinct reflective-panel alternative to the olive DMG default.
GBC response and color, a saturation lift, then the cgwg subpixel grid so the panel reads as a GBC LCD
doc.passes: Colour passes stay at the native 160x144, unfiltered, and only the grid renders at the viewport: lcd-grid-v2 takes its LCD cell from its source size, so a viewport-sized source turns one cell into one screen pixel (no grid, flat lifted blacks, 1-px subpixel streaks). This is the upstream nds/3ds-lcd-grid-v2 structure.
doc.params: Tuned on settled frames, with the core's own correction off (config/systems/gbc/shaders.json), so GBC colours pass this matrix once. lighten_screen 0.5 is Gambatte's default central frontlight (gamma 1.7), the brightness its correction used to add. Image-adjustment only lifts saturation: target gamma 2.2 equals its monitor gamma, so no per-channel gamma lift washes colours out (0.85 did, and saturation 3.0 then pushed HSV saturation past 1: 224,64,64 and 224,96,96 drew alike and orange drew red), and black level 0 keeps every base of its pow() at or above 0. Saturation 1.3 keeps every colour of the clip and bars cards under HSV saturation 1 after this matrix (the bars card's blue, the most saturated, at 0.90). Each lcd-grid-v2 channel lights its own third of a cell, so white needs light from the neighbours or clipped peaks: the subpixels leak 0.45 and gain 1.45 bring white to about 228 (224 at 4K) with about half of the red and green subpixel peaks at 255 and the row gaps and colour stripes still drawn. Red and green subpixels at 0.96 and blue at 0.88 keep the white slightly warm. blacklevel and ambient 0 keep black black.

doc.params: The same grid as gbc/screen.slangp, tuned on settled frames, with mGBA's own correction pinned off (config/systems/gba/shaders.json). Image-adjustment only lifts saturation: target gamma 2.2 equals its monitor gamma, so no per-channel gamma lift washes colours out (1.2 did, and saturation 2.6 then pushed HSV saturation past 1 so 224,64,64 and 224,96,96 drew alike), and black level 0 keeps every base of its pow() at or above 0. Subpixels leaking 0.45 with gain 1.38 give a white of about 226 with the row gaps and stripes still drawn; red and green subpixels 0.96 and blue 0.88 keep it slightly warm. blacklevel and ambient 0 take the lift off black (54 before).

doc.why: Retro Crisis GDV-NTSC, SNES RGB 100 (720p Steam Deck): guest.r's crt-guest-advanced-ntsc from the pinned libretro tree with Retro Crisis's own Steam Deck (720p) values (GPL-3.0, github.com/RetroCrisis/Retro-Crisis-GDV-NTSC, as imported by ShaderGlass), the look the owner chose for Semu's CRTs (2026-10-04).
doc.params: His values as published, float noise rounded, except: the hum bar (barintensity, barspeed) is left out, since a rolling band is the fault the owner reported; any overscan crop (overscanX) is left out, since Semu places the picture at whole steps; and ShaderGlass's own blendMode is not a shader parameter. intres 1 draws a frame of 336 lines or more at round(lines/224) lines per scanline, so an interlaced high-resolution mode keeps the 240-line scanlines, and changes nothing below. Since M16 this 1 is only the fallback: the renderer sets intres for each screen at run time (RendererScanlinePitch), so a 480-line mode draws 480 scanlines at a whole step, which reverses the M14 ruling of 240 scanlines for 480-line modes (reversible: drop the renderer's set_param). interm 0: guest's Interlace Mode (default 2) bobs a field per frame from 375 lines, and every emulator hands over whole progressive frames. ntsc_fields 1 (his preset has 0): unmerged, ntsc-pass1 flips the chroma phase every frame (mod(FrameCount, 2.0)), a 30 Hz shimmer on coloured edges and dithering measured on the render host; merged, both phases are averaged into one steady frame, as his Mega Drive preset does.

3DS top screen: the crisp lcd1x grid at its brightest, the parallax-barrier panel reads sharper than the touch panel

3DS touch screen: the panel's light without a drawn pixel grid. The shell's bottom opening holds 320x240 at a fractional scale on every display (0.95x on the Deck, 1.4x at 1080p, 2.8x at 4K), where lcd1x's one-sine-per-game-pixel grid beats against the screen's pixels: top.slangp drew 18-px vertical and horizontal bands there (column profile 146..238 on a white card). Below one screen pixel per game pixel no grid can be resolved anyway.
doc.passes: Image-adjustment runs at the native 320x240 and sharp-bilinear-simple resamples it to the screen: it samples each game pixel at its texel centre and filters only a band 1/max(floor(scale), 1) texel wide where two pixels meet. At a whole multiple, which the computed dual layouts use (1x to 5x), that is pixel exact; at the shell's 0.95x and 1.42x the band is the whole texel, plain bilinear, so no one-pixel line drops out (nearest sampling dropped 4 of 80 columns and 2 of 30 rows at 0.95x); at 2.84x it is half a texel, so a line card has half as many in-between pixels. Bilinear at viewport scale blurred every pixel of the computed layouts: a one-pixel line drew 4 px wide at 2x, peak 143 of 191.
doc.params: ia_luminance 0.75 is the mean of top.slangp's grid ((4/5) x (16/17)), so both screens keep the same brightness

doc.why: DS screens: the NDS-tuned lcd1x grid
doc.params: BRIGHTEN_LCD 12 keeps the column grid at +-7.7% instead of upstream's +-20%. The shell places both screens at the fractional fit scale (2.2x on the Deck), where a grid near two pixels a cell beats against the panel's pixel grid into 11-px vertical bands; the shallow grid keeps that beat below sight.

doc.why: Retro Crisis GDV-NTSC, Dreamcast - Clean (720p Steam Deck): guest.r's crt-guest-advanced-ntsc from the pinned libretro tree with Retro Crisis's own Steam Deck values for the Dreamcast (GPL-3.0, github.com/RetroCrisis/Retro-Crisis-GDV-NTSC, as imported by ShaderGlass), M16's rule for every TV console: his preset for the console's cleanest stock signal (the Dreamcast's RGB and VGA: Clean, not Dirty).
doc.params: His values as published, except: ntsc_fields 1 (his preset has 0): unmerged, ntsc-pass1 flips the chroma phase every frame, a 30 Hz shimmer on coloured edges; merged, both phases are averaged into one steady frame. interm 0: guest's Interlace Mode bobs a field per frame from 375 lines, and every emulator hands over whole progressive frames. intres is the static fallback only: the renderer sets it for each screen (RendererScanlinePitch) so every scanline spans whole output rows, one scanline per line at a whole step (2 rows each at 2x), round(scale) rows at a fractional one (400 scanlines of 2 rows for a 480-line picture on 800 rows), never a 240-line look on a 480-line picture. His static intres is 1.5 (320 scanlines for 480 lines, 2.25 rows each at 720p), which on the Deck's whole-step 1x would fall 1.5 rows apart and beat.
